newsitem.title: UK: Cash Brent improves, Urals and Nigerian also rise.
newsitem.headline: Cash Brent improves, Urals and Nigerian also rise.

text.p: Cash Brent markets rose on Wednesday as buyers re-entered the market encouraged by cold weather and heating oil demand.
Intermonth spreads and CFD values were bid higher and Dated Brent discounts narrowed despite the weight of a continued CFD play.
Brent spreads all gained about five cents from closing levels on Tuesday with Dec/Jan at +34 cents and Jan/Feb at +50 cents.
CFDs moved up 5-10 cents for the next three weeks with next week at Jan -2 cts.
Dated Brent traded twice on Wednesday morning at widely divergent levels but dealers said the higher number was probably a truer reflection of market sentiment.
Dec 2-4 Brent was sold by a U.S. trader at Dec -45 cents following a series of sales by the same company since last week at Dec -48 cents.
The sale was quickly followed by a Dec 3-5 deal at Dec -33 cents from a European trader who picked up the cargo late on Tuesday at Dec -40 cents.
Dealers said recent lower Brent trades were part of a swaps related trading strategy on the Brent CFD market.
"Fundamentals should definitely value Brent in the thirties now," said one trader.

Forties and Oseberg both showed signs of improvement after sales at higher levels in the last couple of days and the charter by refiners on Wednesday of tankers for a million barrels of each for the U.S., loading Dec 1-3.
But Statfjord and Ekofisk remained under pressure.
Evidence of better demand in the Atlantic Basin also came from better values for Nigerian Forcados in a trade on Tuesday at Dated Brent +65 cents. Earlier December cargoes are put nearer +60.
